data: From Mughaliyah Saltanat to Sovereign Republic: India in Transition

This course studies the history of India from the death of Emperor Aurangzeb in 1707 to the founding of the Republic of India in 1950. The collapse of the Mughal Empire was followed by a period of competition between various rising powers including the Sikhs, the Marathas, Hyderabad and the Europeans, which eventually resulted in the emergence of the British Raj in India. British colonial rule transformed India. It changed what it meant to be Indian and led to new ways of thinking about nation, religion, and what it meant to be modern. The collapse of British rule in India in 1947 was accompanied by immense violence and lead to the creation of two new countries; India and Pakistan. This course will focus on six key themes; the contest for power among the successors to the Mughal Empire, the rebellion of 1857, the history of the Indian princes, the emergence of Indian nationalism, the two world wars and finally the making of an independent India. The course will prove useful to students interested in Indian history and politics.
